subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The radius of a sphere is increased from 7 cm to 7.02 cm. Find the approximate increase in the volume of the sphere.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), book p.211, chapter 10 APPLICATIONS OF DERIVATIVES, the ERRORS AND APPROXIMATIONS sub-section, Very Short Answer question 7. The answer was checked before it was written: the exact increase (4/3)π[(7.02)³ − 7³] = 3.9312π cm³ against the approximation 3.92π cm³, a difference of under 0.3%.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what dr is here, and what the derivative of the volume formula turns out to be.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write dV = 4πr² · dr
steps.margin_note: First mark. The radius is given directly this time, so no halving is needed: dr is simply 7.02 − 7. The 3 from the power cancels the 3 in the denominator.
steps.memory_tip: Differentiating (4/3)πr³ gives 4πr², which is the surface-area formula.
lines: Let r be the radius and V = (4/3)πr³ the volume of the sphere.
Here r = 7 cm and dr = 7.02 − 7 = 0.02 cm

recall.must_convey: That r = 7, dr = 0.02, and that differentiating V = (4/3)πr³ gives dV = 4πr²·dr.

steps.why: dV = (dV/dr)·dr is the approximation being used. The derivative of (4/3)πr³ is 4πr², so the whole question reduces to one substitution once this line is on the page.
common_mistakes: Taking dr = 7.02 instead of the difference 0.02.
Leaving the (4/3) in front and writing dV = (4/3)πr²·dr.

steps.label: Substitute r = 7 and dr = 0.02
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 4 × 49 × 0.02 = 3.92, so the answer is 3.92π cm³. Keep π in the answer; the decimal is an extra, not a replacement.
steps.memory_tip: 4 × 49 = 196, and 196 × 0.02 = 3.92. The unit is cm³ because it is a volume.

lines.text: ∴ the volume increases by approximately 3.92π cm³ ≈ 12.32 cm³

recall.must_convey: That substituting gives dV = 3.92π cm³, about 12.32 cm³.

steps.why: The exact increase is (4/3)π[(7.02)³ − 7³] = 3.9312π cm³, and the approximation gives 3.92π cm³. They agree to three figures because dr = 0.02 is small compared with r = 7, which is the condition the method needs. The answer here is the change itself, in cm³; had a percentage been asked, the relative form dV/V = 3(dr/r) would be used, because the volume is r to the power 3.
common_mistakes: Writing the unit as cm² instead of cm³.
Computing the two full volumes and subtracting, which is exact but is not what 'approximate' asks for.
